body:
**Draft: validation is incomplete; a hard review is running.** Fixes D-TREE-THRASH1.

## The problem

A fresh detached writer got its tree on its first admission look, before placement decided anything. So one open lane cut a tree for every waiting job in its route, and the next hold made those jobs `unprepared` again and C-6.20's sweep gave the trees back. On 2026-11-06, from 05:00Z to 09:20Z, the host's lane controller made 71 releases while 19 jobs waited. Only 4 attempts got reserved, and the store recorded 571 `job.worktree_given_back` events (`why: "no lane"`) across 12 jobs. Each release's swing of trees (median 2.5 GB of free disk) tripped the controller's disk brake about 16 s later.

## The change

A fresh detached writer with no tree now runs the route's ordinary checks against its future tree path. When every check passes (FIFO, caps, probe approval, leases, retention fences, the ramp), `_WorkspaceNeeded` rolls the transaction back, Git prepares the tree outside the store lock, and the same evaluation enters the checks again. `_route_stands` accounts for changes in between, and preparation spends no route retry. Existing trees, retries, in-place jobs, pushes and turns keep their old path. If a lane closes during Git and no lane can take the job, the job waits with its tree marked `unprepared`, and the existing sweep gives the tree back. The race read uses the cached desktop answer (`refresh=False`), so no registry refresh runs inside the store transaction.

No event field or refusal is new. Contract: C-6.20, C-6.8, C-6.10, C-6.11 and C-23.16, with a change-log line.

## Invariants

- **I1, cuts follow placements.** A pass cuts no more trees than it reserves, plus at most one per pass for the labelled race in which a lane closes between evaluation and reservation. A hold before the placement check prevents a cut.
- **I2, order unchanged.** Valid workspaces and the same rows give the same `(job, lane)` reservation order as base. Intended differences: a workspace error surfaces when placement first permits preparation, and a lane hold that arrives mid-pass stops further cuts.
- **I3, a started job has its tree.** Preparation runs from submit's recorded HEAD and captures the baseline before reservation; the recheck never bypasses preparation.
- **I4, no Git for a waiter.** A fresh job whose placement checks leave it waiting runs no workspace Git and cuts no tree.
- **I5, holds unchanged.** C-6.9's FIFO and lease order, C-6.10's capacity clock, C-6.11's labels, C-23.16's demand, C-6.17's disk door and C-8.4's retirement fences.
- **I6, a failing workspace still fails.** C-6.8's refusal, transient backoff and exhaustion still apply, possibly later than the first look; deferral spends no workspace retry and clears no failure count.

Tests: `tests/fake/test_admission_tree_thrash.py` (examples and Hypothesis properties, with I2 compared against base's own method loaded from the base object) and `tests/fake/test_admission_tree_thrash_head.py` (twenty real-Git rounds on head alone).

## Base against head

Synthetic 300-job admission passes (`tools/benchmark_tree_thrash.py`, synthetic workspaces):

| Pass | Preparations | Reservations | Evaluations | Retired instructions | Wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Controller holds after two reservations | 300 → 2 | 2 → 2 | 300 → 300 | −1.42% | +3.78% |
| Every lane open | 300 → 300 | 300 → 300 | 300 → 300 | +27.49% | +20.12% |
| Every lane closed | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | −5.64% (median of two pairs, noisy) | −13.48% |

With every lane open the change costs more: the second set of checks after preparation adds store reads (9,007 → 12,307) and 25.63% more thread CPU. It runs no second route evaluation.

Real Git, twenty two-start rounds; both runs stopped at the build's deadline, so these counts are partial:
- head, after 16 rounds: 42 submitted, 32 reservations, 32 trees present, 0 give-backs;
- base, in its 6th round: 20 submitted, 12 reservations, 18 trees present, 40 give-backs.

Mutants: 5 of 5 executed mutants failed their named tests, after 4 healthy controls passed. The 3 I3 mutants are defined but didn't run.

## Validation so far

The build ran with host load often above 100, and Git there exceeded its 60 s limits:
- required suite: its last run had 49 passes, then 3 failures stopped it, each in submit on `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` past 60 s;
- the new module: 14 passed and 0 failed; 3 cases didn't finish (`test_measured_shape_twenty_two_start_rounds_cut_only_the_forty_placed_trees`, `test_a_hold_after_the_second_reservation_stops_later_cuts_in_this_pass`, `test_i3_generated_head_movements_keep_the_submitted_tree_and_baseline`);
- `test_test_module_names.py` and `test_invariants_index.py`: 26 passed.

The new module's fixture alone sets `workspace_git_timeout_s` and `worktree_add_timeout_s` to 300 s; production limits stay as they were. CI runs the whole suite.

Review r1 (hard tier, GPT-6.1 Sol): lane job `20261106-135510-tt-review-r1`, dispatched 18:55Z 11/06. It runs the three unfinished cases, the head test, the required suite and the three I3 mutants, and checks I1-I6, the lane-close race and the cost against the code.

## Provenance

Lane job `20261106-044747-tree-thrash-build` (GPT-6.1 Sol) built this. Git denied the lane its `index.lock`, so the hub took the files from its salvage commit `a0ba58e2d` after checking all 39 paths byte for byte against the job worktree. It left out five scratch logs at the repo root. The report is `docs/reports/2026-11-06-tree-thrash.md`.

The change takes effect at the next install. The host's disk lines moved to hold 62 / open 67 on 11/06, partly because of this defect; the hub tells their owner when this installs.
